sources.title: Fluorinated gas (F gas): guidance for users, producers and traders
facts: Environment Agency and Defra collection covers HFCs, PFCs and SF6 and links rules for users, producers, traders, quota and equipment.
A regulatory collection identifies scope and obligations but is not a measured emissions record for a parcel.

sources.title: Calculate the carbon dioxide equivalent quantity of an F gas
facts: Official guidance calculates F-gas CO2 equivalent from gas mass multiplied by global warming potential.
A CO2e conversion calculation requires a supported gas mass and does not by itself establish an observed release to atmosphere.

sources.title: Applying for quota to produce or import F gas
facts: Great Britain HFC quota is allocated for placing bulk HFCs on the market and is expressed in CO2-equivalent tonnes.
Quota allocation or use is an administrative market quantity and is not physical emissions from a parcel.

sources.title: Recovering, reclaiming and recycling F gas
facts: Guidance distinguishes recovery, recycling and reclamation of F gases from refrigeration, fire protection, switchgear, aerosols and solvents.
Recovered or reclaimed gas mass is not equivalent to atmospheric emissions without evidence of an actual release.

sources.title: Record and report F gas and equipment pre-charged with F gas
facts: The guidance requires records and reports for specified production, import, export, destruction, feedstock and pre-charged-equipment activities.
Reported market or activity quantities must not be treated as parcel emissions unless an applicable emissions observation or method supports that conversion.

sources.title: Fluorinated gases (F gases)
facts: Official guidance lists F-gas types and global warming potentials used for regulatory CO2e calculations.
A GWP reference factor is not an observed emissions amount and cannot substitute for activity or release data.

sources.title: Moving F gas between Great Britain and Northern Ireland
facts: Guidance distinguishes Great Britain and Northern Ireland quota, registry, customs and reporting requirements for HFC movements.
A cross-border movement or customs declaration is not an atmospheric emissions measurement.

sources.title: Qualifications to work with F gas
facts: Environment Agency and Defra guidance sets qualification requirements for people handling F gases in relevant equipment.
Qualification or compliance status does not quantify emissions from equipment, a facility or a parcel.

sources.title: Uses of F gas (HFCs) exempt from the phase down
facts: The guidance identifies HFC uses exempt from Great Britain's phase-down and associated labelling and reporting requirements.
An exemption from quota phase-down is a regulatory classification, not evidence of atmospheric release.

sources.title: Import, export or manufacture equipment pre-charged with F gas
facts: Guidance covers quota authorisations, declarations of conformity, reporting and labelling for equipment pre-charged with HFCs.
Gas contained in equipment or quota-backed equipment imports must not be assumed to have been emitted.

sources.title: Bans on F gas in new products and equipment: current and future
facts: Official guidance lists F-gas product and equipment bans by use, gas and global warming potential.
A product ban threshold or lifecycle criterion is regulatory evidence, not an observed parcel emissions value.

sources.title: Banned F gas for refilling equipment
facts: Guidance gives refill restrictions for high-GWP F gases and distinguishes reclaimed and recycled gas options.
A refill restriction, GWP or equipment charge does not prove a release to atmosphere.

sources.title: Company certification to work with F gas
facts: Official guidance requires company certification for specified work on equipment containing F gas and distinguishes company and individual requirements.
Certification status is compliance metadata and not a physical emissions measurement.

sources.title: Selling F gas in cylinders or equipment
facts: Guidance covers sale of F gas in cylinders or equipment, customer certification checks and sales records.
A sale quantity or customer record is market activity and cannot be promoted directly to parcel emissions.

sources.title: Transfer and authorise F gas quota to another business
facts: Quota holders may transfer quota, authorise equipment importers or delegate quota authorisations within the annual quota system.
Transferred or authorised quota is an administrative entitlement and not a measured greenhouse-gas release.

sources.title: Pollution Inventory - National Data Library
facts: Environment Agency Pollution Inventory data collates annual mass releases and transfers from large regulated industrial sites, including point and fugitive sources.
Facility or permit-wide annual releases are not automatically attributable to an individual cadastral parcel without verified facility-to-parcel binding.

sources.title: Pollution inventory reporting forms
facts: Environment Agency forms allow regulated operators to report emissions to air, land and controlled waters plus wastewater and waste transfers.
A reporting form or blank reporting field is not itself an observed emissions result.

sources.title: Pollution inventory reporting collection
facts: The Environment Agency collection explains Pollution Inventory reporting for regulated industrial activities and annual releases/transfers.
Collection and permit-reporting scope must remain distinct from parcel-level measurement.

sources.title: CCUS: Ensuring fair access to CO2 infrastructure
facts: DESNZ consultation reviewed access to carbon-dioxide transport and storage infrastructure and closed in February 2026.
Consultation proposals and access rights are policy evidence, not observed captured, transported, stored or emitted CO2 quantities.

sources.title: CCUS fair access consultation accessible webpage
facts: The accessible consultation record describes third-party access questions for CO2 transport and storage networks.
Infrastructure access or policy pathways do not establish physical emissions or removals for a parcel.

sources.title: CCUS: non-pipeline transport consultation
facts: DESNZ sought views on support, costs, regulation and operation of non-pipeline CO2 transport for CCUS chains.
Prospective CO2 transport routes and support mechanisms are not observations of atmospheric emissions or permanent storage.

sources.title: CCUS non-pipeline transport consultation accessible webpage
facts: The accessible NPT consultation sets out proposed delivery, cost, risk, regulation and operational options for transporting CO2 outside pipelines.
A consultation data template or prospective project description is not a verified emissions or removals measurement.

sources.title: Carbon dioxide transport and storage: regulatory instructions and guidance
facts: Ofgem RIGs specify regulatory and financial information reporting for licensed CO2 transport and storage networks and were updated to version 2.0.
Regulatory reporting packs and financial information do not by themselves prove captured, stored or emitted CO2 at parcel level.

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for installations: how to comply
facts: Environment Agency and DESNZ guidance covers UK ETS obligations for installations with greenhouse-gas emissions permits and was updated for METS and 2026 allocation changes.
A permit, compliance obligation or allowance calculation is not itself a parcel emissions measurement.

sources.title: Voluntary monitoring, reporting and verification period for waste incineration
facts: Environment Agency guidance describes the voluntary MRV-only period for energy-from-waste and waste-incineration facilities ahead of future UK ETS expansion.
Participation in a voluntary MRV period or future scheme scope is not itself an observed parcel emissions quantity.
